title: Revisiting Deep Learning Models for Tabular Data
why_relevant: Defines strong, simple deep baselines for tabular data (tabular ResNet and FT-Transformer) and emphasizes consistent training protocols; directly applicable to an all-numeric Kaggle multiclass problem.
extracted_technique: Train tabular ResNet/FT-Transformer with careful regularization, consistent preprocessing for numeric features, and robust evaluation; no assumption that DL always beats GBDT.
takeaway: Use paper-backed tabular ResNet and/or FT-Transformer as high-capacity supervised backbones, then ensemble across folds/seeds for stability.

title: Self-Supervised Learning using Denoising Autoencoders - PyTorch Tabular
why_relevant: Provides a concrete, reproducible recipe for DAE-style self-supervised pretraining on tabular features, which matches top Kaggle tabular patterns and can improve downstream classification.
extracted_technique: Pretrain a DAE by corrupting inputs (noise/masking) and reconstructing; then fine-tune a supervised model using learned representations.
query: denoising autoencoder pretraining tabular data classification
takeaway: A DAE pretraining stage is practical and can be implemented leak-free (label-free) before supervised CV training; keep it toggleable for runtime.

title: Tabular Playground Series - Feb 2022 [tabular data] - Standings - CLIST
why_relevant: Gives an external snapshot of final leaderboard difficulty (scores around 0.99), setting a realistic target for model capacity and ensembling.
extracted_technique: Use leaderboard difficulty to justify multi-seed, multi-fold ensembling and higher-capacity deep models rather than a single baseline.
takeaway: Target should be near 0.99 accuracy; plan must include strong models + careful validation + ensembling to be competitive.
